source_book: Sri Chaitanya — IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students, Physics (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring: VSAQ 17, SAQ 16 numbered questions (31 entries after splitting printed parts), LAQ 6 numbered (7 entries), PROBLEM 11 — 66 entries. The FORMULAE block on scan p.56 (printed p.58, left column) is not indexed. The question numbers of VSAQ 6 (scan p.57) and SAQ 14 (scan p.63) are cropped at the left margin of the scan and were assigned by sequence; printed typos are noted per entry. Stems are restated in our own wording; no solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy.

chapter.printed_title: SYSTEM OF PARTICLES AND ROTATIONAL MOTION

questions.stem: How can you tell a hard-boiled egg from a raw egg by spinning each egg on a table top?
Why must a helicopter have two propellers?
Why is it easier to balance a bicycle while it is moving?
A door cannot be opened or closed by applying a force at its hinges. Explain why.

A child sits still at one end of a long trolley that moves uniformly with speed V on a smooth horizontal floor. If the child stands up and runs about on the trolley in any manner, what is the speed of the centre of mass of the (trolley + child) system?
Newton's laws of motion apply to the individual particles of a system. Justify that the motion of the system as a whole can also be described using Newton's laws.
questions.notes: The question number is cropped at the left margin of the scan; assigned 6 by sequence (between 5 and 7).

questions.stem: In which of the following cases does the centre of mass of a body coincide with its geometric centre? (a) The density decreases continuously from right to left. (b) The density decreases from left to right up to the centre and then increases in the same proportion.
questions.notes: The printed (a)/(b) are the two cases to choose between, not separate sub-questions, so this is one entry.

questions.stem: Why does a bicycle wheel have spokes?
Define radius of gyration. State the factors on which it depends.
Explain how a diver who jumps into water from a height is able to make a loop in the air.
If the polar ice caps of the Earth melted, what would happen to the length of the day?
The stone of a hand flour grinder has its handle near the rim. Give the reason.
questions.notes: Printed 'hand flow grinder' — read as 'hand flour grinder'.

questions.stem: It is easier to turn a steering wheel of larger diameter than one of smaller diameter. Give the reason.
questions.notes: Printed 'It is easier to then the streaming wheel of a larger diameter' — read as 'to turn the steering wheel'.

questions.stem: A jack screw has a long arm. Explain why.
A person sits near the edge of a circular platform that turns with uniform angular speed. What change occurs in the motion of the platform?
questions.notes: AMBIGUOUS DATUM. The printed stem never says what the person does; the book's treatment assumes the person moves from the edge toward the centre of the platform. A card should state that movement explicitly.

questions.stem: State the factors on which the moment of inertia of a body depends.
Define centripetal force and write its formula.
What is meant by the centre of mass of a system? Obtain the expression for the centre of mass of a system of two particles.
questions.notes: Printed as one numbered question: define centre of mass, obtain the expression for (a) two particles and (b) a large number of particles, and give its physical significance. Split per printed part; the definition is placed with (a) and the significance with (b). Printed 'Centre of mass use of a system' (typo).

questions.stem: Obtain the expression for the centre of mass of a system of a large number of particles. What is the physical significance of the centre of mass of a system?
questions.notes: Second printed part of SAQ 1; see saq1a for the split.

questions.stem: Show that the velocity of the centre of mass of a moving isolated system stays constant when no external force acts on it.
questions.notes: Printed 'in the absence of external free' — read as 'external force'.

questions.stem: The state of the centre of mass of a system does not change when no external force acts. Explain this with an example.
Give four examples of the motion of the centre of mass.
questions.notes: Printed 'Give four examples of Centre of Mass of motion' — read as 'motion of the centre of mass'.

questions.stem: The net force on a system of particles is zero. What is the acceleration of the centre of mass?
The net force on a system of particles is zero. What is the momentum of the centre of mass?
The net force on a system of particles is zero. What is the velocity of the centre of mass?
The net force on a system of particles is zero. What is the velocity of an individual particle of the system?
State the differences between centre of mass and centre of gravity.
Show that a system of particles moving under an external force moves as if the force were applied at its centre of mass.
Explain the centre of mass of the Earth–Moon system and how this system moves around the Sun.
questions.notes: The book prints a figure of the Sun, the Earth, the Moon and their common centre of mass beside the answer; the question does not depend on it.

questions.stem: Define angular velocity ω. Derive the relation v = rω.
Define angular acceleration and torque. Derive the relation between angular acceleration and torque.
Write the equations of motion for a particle rotating about a fixed axis.
Write the expression for torque.
Write the expression for angular momentum.
questions.notes: Printed 'Angular nomentum' (typo).

questions.stem: Write the expression for rotational power.
Write the expression for rotational kinetic energy.
Write the expression for the moment of inertia of a solid sphere of radius R about its diameter.
Write the expression for the moment of inertia of a circular ring of radius R about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to its plane.
Write the expression for the moment of inertia of a disc of radius R about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to its plane.
Write the expression for the moment of inertia of a solid cylinder of length l and radius R about an axis through its centre and perpendicular to its length.
Draw the graph between moment of inertia and radius of gyration.
questions.notes: The question number is cropped at the left margin of the scan; assigned 14 by sequence (between 13 and 15).

questions.stem: Draw the graph between rotational kinetic energy and angular velocity.
Draw the graph between angular momentum and angular velocity.
Draw the graph between angular momentum and kinetic energy of rotation.
State and prove the parallel axes theorem.
A thin flat circular disk has radius of gyration k about a diameter taken as the axis. The disk is cut along a diameter AB into two equal pieces. Find the radius of gyration of each piece about AB.
questions.notes: Depends on a figure: a disk drawn with a diameter AB across it (the cut line).

questions.stem: State and prove the perpendicular axes theorem.
A thin circular ring and a thin flat circular disk of the same mass have the same moment of inertia about their respective diameters taken as axes. Find the ratio of their radii.
questions.notes: The book prints no working for this part (b); only part (a) is worked.

questions.stem: State and prove the principle of conservation of angular momentum. Explain the principle of conservation of angular momentum with examples.
Derive the expression for the moment of inertia of a thin rectangular lamina about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the lamina and passing through one of its corners.
A 50 kg mass is lifted using a 1 metre long lever. If the length of the lever is reduced by 20%, how much more or less force must be applied to produce the same torque?

A mechanic applies a force of 100 N at the end of a spanner to tighten a bolt. The spanner is 0.5 m long. How much torque acts on the bolt? If the mechanic increases the applied force by 20% but holds the spanner closer, at 0.4 m, does the torque increase or decrease?
questions.notes: Printed 'How much torque is existed on the bolt' and 'If the machine increases the force' — read as 'is exerted' and 'the mechanic'.

questions.stem: Find the moment of inertia of a sphere about a tangent to the sphere, given that the moment of inertia of the sphere about any of its diameters is 2MR²/5, where M is the mass of the sphere and R is its radius.
questions.notes: Printed as '5. a)' but no part (b) is printed anywhere; the part label is kept as printed.

questions.stem: Find the moment of inertia of a circular ring about a tangent lying in its plane.
Find the moment of inertia of a circular ring about a tangent perpendicular to its plane.
Two spheres of masses 6 kg and 3 kg move along the same line with speeds 3 m/s and 6 m/s, away from each other. Find the velocity of the centre of mass.
questions.notes: Printed 'spheares'. A figure beside the question shows the 6 kg sphere moving to the left at 3 m/s and the 3 kg sphere moving to the right at 6 m/s.

questions.stem: Two masses of 2 kg each have velocities v1 = 4i + 2j and v2 = 2i + 3j. Find the velocity of the centre of mass.
A flywheel of moment of inertia 50 kg·m² and radius 2 m is accelerated by a tangential force of magnitude 10 N. Find the angular velocity 4 seconds after the start.

An acrobat spins about a vertical axis at 160 rpm with his arms folded. By folding his hands further, the moment of inertia about the axis of rotation decreases by 20%. Calculate the new rate of rotation.
questions.notes: Printed 'verticle axis' (typo).

questions.stem: Three particles, each of mass 100 g, are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side 10 cm. Find the moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the centroid of the triangle and perpendicular to its plane.

Four particles, each of mass 100 g, are placed at the corners of a square of side 10 cm. Find the moment of inertia of the system about an axis passing through the centre of the square and perpendicular to its plane. Also find the radius of gyration of the system.
Find the kinetic energy of a circular disc of mass 5 kg and radius 1 m that rotates at 60 rpm about an axis passing through a point on its circumference and perpendicular to its plane.
A flywheel making 300 revolutions per minute has a moment of inertia of 0.3 kg·m². Find the torque needed to bring it to rest in 20 s.
When 100 J of work is done on a flywheel, its angular velocity increases from 60 rpm to 180 rpm. What is the moment of inertia of the wheel?
questions.notes: The book prints a bracketed answer value after the stem; it is not copied here.

questions.stem: A wheel rotates at 50 rpm on a shaft. A second identical wheel, initially at rest, is suddenly coupled to the same shaft. What is the speed of the combined wheels?
questions.notes: PRINTED DEFECT (probable). The stem reads 50 rpm, but the book's own working takes the initial speed as 500 rpm, so the printed stem and its answer disagree. Founder decision needed on which value a card should use. Printed 'whell' and 'indentical' (typos).

questions.stem: The radius of gyration of a uniform thin rod of length L about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through a point on the rod is equal to the radius of gyration of the rod about its centre. Find the distance of this axis from the centre of the rod.
questions.notes: Printed 'uniform thin road' and 'of the road' — read as 'rod'.
